flat_db_bench.name: Flat DB Bench Press

video.title: The Dumbbell Bench Press: Gym Shorts (How To)

flat_db_bench.referenceNote: The foundation chest builder — dumbbells allow a deeper stretch than a barbell and fix left-right imbalances.
setup: Sit on the flat bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh.
Kick the weights up with your knees as you lie back.
Plant feet flat, pinch shoulder blades together with a slight arch.
Start with dumbbells above your chest, wrists straight.
flat_db_bench.tempo: 2-1-2 — 2 seconds down, 1 second pause on the chest, 2 seconds up.
dos: Keep elbows at roughly 45 degrees to your torso
Drive your feet into the floor for full-body tension
Lower until you feel a deep chest stretch
Keep shoulder blades pinched the whole set
donts: Do not flare elbows out to 90 degrees
Do not bounce the weights off your chest
Do not clang the dumbbells together at the top
Do not lift your hips off the bench
mistakes: Pressing with elbows flared wide, stressing the shoulders
Half reps that never reach chest level
Losing the shoulder-blade pinch mid-set
flat_db_bench.tip: Think about bending the dumbbell handles outward as you press — it keeps the chest engaged and elbows in the safe zone.

incline_db_press.name: Incline DB Press
incline_db_press.referenceNote: Targets the upper chest — a 30-degree incline keeps tension on the pecs instead of shifting it to the shoulders.
setup: Set the bench to about 30 degrees — one notch above flat.
Rest dumbbells on your thighs, kick up and lie back.
Feet flat, shoulder blades pinched, slight arch.
Start with dumbbells at upper-chest level.
incline_db_press.tempo: 2-1-2 — controlled down, brief squeeze, powerful press.
dos: Keep the 30-degree angle — steeper shifts work to shoulders
Press up and slightly inward in an arc
Squeeze the chest for a beat at the top
Control the full stretch at the bottom
donts: Do not set the bench past 45 degrees
Do not let the dumbbells drift outward
Do not rush the lowering phase
Do not over-arch your back
mistakes: Too steep a bench turning it into a shoulder press
Cutting range short to lift heavier
Letting wrists bend back under the load
incline_db_press.tip: Mark your bench's 30-degree notch with tape so setup is instant every session.

standing_ohp.name: Standing DB Overhead Press
standing_ohp.referenceNote: Builds the front and side delts while your core works overtime to keep you stable.
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, dumbbells at shoulder height.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Ribs down — do not lean back.
Press straight overhead until arms are nearly straight.
standing_ohp.tempo: 2-1-2 — no bouncing out of the bottom.
dos: Squeeze glutes hard before every rep
Press the weights in a straight vertical line
Keep wrists stacked over elbows
Lower all the way to shoulder height
donts: Do not arch your lower back to cheat the weight up
Do not shrug the weights with your traps
Do not bang dumbbells together overhead
Do not hold your breath for the whole set
mistakes: Leaning back turns it into an incline chest press
Using leg drive to bounce the weight up
Stopping the press at forehead height
standing_ohp.tip: If your lower back complains, do it seated with back support — same delts, less cheating.

lateral_raise.name: Lateral Raises

video.title: Dumbbell Lateral Raise: Gym Shorts (How To)

lateral_raise.referenceNote: The width builder — strict form with light weight beats heavy swinging every time.
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in.
Slight bend in the elbows — keep it fixed.
Lean forward just a touch.
Raise out to the sides until arms reach shoulder height.
dos: Lead with your elbows, not your hands
Stop at shoulder height
Keep the motion slightly in front of the side plane
Control the negative for a full 3 seconds
donts: Do not swing the weights up with momentum
Do not shrug your traps toward your ears
Do not raise above shoulder height
Do not use a weight you cannot pause with
mistakes: Turning it into a full-body heave
Lifting the arms too far forward (becomes a front raise)
Dropping the weights instead of lowering them
lateral_raise.tip: Do the last set as a drop set — cut the weight in half and keep going to failure for extra side-delt growth.

oh_triceps_ext.name: Overhead Triceps Extension

video.title: Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension — proper technique

oh_triceps_ext.referenceNote: Stretches the long head of the triceps like nothing else — the key to bigger arms.
setup: Hold one dumbbell with both hands, arms extended overhead.
Keep upper arms close to your head, elbows pointing up.
Brace your core, ribs down.
Lower the weight behind your head by bending only the elbows.
dos: Keep upper arms perfectly still
Lower until you feel a deep triceps stretch
Squeeze hard at the top without harsh lockout
Use a weight you can control behind your head
donts: Do not let elbows flare wide
Do not arch your back under the load
Do not cut the range short
Do not rush — the stretch is the point
mistakes: Moving the whole arm instead of just the forearm
Going too heavy and turning it into a shoulder workout
Skipping the bottom stretch
oh_triceps_ext.tip: Seated with back support removes all cheating — try it when your lower back wants to join in.

hanging_knee_raise.name: Hanging Knee/Leg Raises

video.title: Hanging Knee Raise Tutorial | Lower-Abs + Stability

hanging_knee_raise.referenceNote: The king of lower-ab exercises — control the swing and your abs do all the work. No pull-up bar at home? Do lying reverse crunches instead.
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar, hands shoulder-width apart.
Let your body settle — no swinging.
Brace your core, ribs down.
Curl your knees up toward your chest, tilting the pelvis.
dos: Pause briefly at the top of each rep
Lower slowly for 3 seconds
Keep the swing completely out of it
Breathe out as you lift the knees
donts: Do not swing to generate momentum
Do not just lift the knees without curling the pelvis
Do not drop down fast
Do not hold your breath
mistakes: Kipping the reps up with body swing
Stopping at 90 degrees without the pelvic curl — that is hip flexors, not abs
Letting the shoulders shrug up to the ears
hanging_knee_raise.tip: When 15 strict reps get easy, straighten the legs a little more each week toward full leg raises.

one_arm_row.name: One-Arm DB Row
one_arm_row.referenceNote: Builds a thick back one side at a time and exposes strength imbalances.
setup: Place one knee and the same-side hand on the bench.
Plant the other foot wide, back flat and parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down from the shoulder.
Pull the elbow up and back toward your hip.
one_arm_row.tempo: 2-1-2 — squeeze the shoulder blade at the top.
dos: Pull toward your hip, not your chest
Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top
Keep your torso square — no twisting
Lower under full control
donts: Do not rotate your torso to heave the weight
Do not shrug the shoulder toward your ear
Do not let your lower back round
Do not rush the stretch at the bottom
mistakes: Twisting the whole body to lift heavier
Pulling with the bicep instead of driving the elbow
Cutting the bottom range short
one_arm_row.tip: Start each set with your weaker side and match reps on the stronger side — imbalances even out fast.

db_rdl.name: DB Romanian Deadlift

video.title: How to do a Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift | Proper Form & Technique | NASM

db_rdl.referenceNote: A hip hinge, not a squat — the best hamstring and glute builder you can do with dumbbells.
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells in front of your thighs, feet hip-width.
Soften the knees and lock that slight bend in.
Push your hips straight back, chest proud.
Lower along your legs until you feel a deep hamstring stretch.
dos: Initiate every rep by pushing the hips back
Keep the dumbbells brushing your legs
Keep your spine neutral throughout
Drive the hips forward and squeeze glutes at the top
donts: Do not round your lower back to go deeper
Do not bend the knees more as you descend
Do not let the weights drift away from your body
Do not hyperextend at the top
mistakes: Squatting the weight down instead of hinging
Chasing depth past a flat back
Feeling it all in the lower back — the hinge pattern needs work
db_rdl.tip: Stand a foot in front of a wall and tap your glutes to it on each rep — instant hinge feedback.

bulgarian_split_squat.name: Bulgarian Split Squat

video.channel: Dr Donald A Ozello DC, NSCA-CPT
video.title: Dumbbell Split Squats AKA Bulgarian Split Squats and Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat

bulgarian_split_squat.referenceNote: Brutal, humbling, and brilliant — builds each leg independently with just dumbbells and a bench.
setup: Stand a stride in front of the bench, back to it.
Rest the top of your rear foot on the bench.
Dumbbells at your sides, torso upright.
Lower straight down until your front thigh is parallel.
dos: Keep your torso upright, chest proud
Drive through the front heel
Let the front knee travel naturally over the toes
Keep 90 percent of the weight on the front leg
donts: Do not push off the rear foot
Do not let the front knee collapse inward
Do not lean far forward
Do not short-change the depth
mistakes: Standing too close or too far from the bench
Staying too light because of balance — go heavier once stable
Bouncing out of the bottom
bulgarian_split_squat.tip: Do all sets on one leg before switching — the pump and the focus are both better.

rear_delt_fly.name: Bent-Over Rear Delt Fly

video.title: Dumbbell Bent Over Rear Delt Fly

rear_delt_fly.referenceNote: The missing piece for 3D shoulders — direct rear-delt work for posture and balance.
setup: Hinge forward until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbells hang under your shoulders, slight elbow bend.
Brace your core, back flat.
Raise the weights out to the sides in a wide arc to shoulder height.
dos: Lead with your elbows
Stop when upper arms reach shoulder height
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top
Use a light weight you can control
donts: Do not swing the torso up for momentum
Do not pull the weights back toward your hips
Do not shrug your traps
Do not go heavy — form dies fast here
mistakes: Using back muscles by pulling too far back
Bouncing out of the bottom position
Letting the lower back round under fatigue
rear_delt_fly.tip: Do these chest-supported (face down on an incline bench) when you want zero cheating.

bicep_curl.name: DB Bicep Curls

video.channel: Fit Father Project - Fitness For Busy Fathers
video.title: Bicep Curls — (DUMBBELL FORM & TECHNIQUE)

bicep_curl.referenceNote: Simple, but only effective when the ego stays out of it — strict curls build strict peaks.
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Pin your elbows to your ribs.
Brace your core.
Curl the weights toward your shoulders.
dos: Keep upper arms completely still
Squeeze hard at the top
Lower for a full 3 seconds
Keep wrists straight
donts: Do not swing the weights up
Do not let elbows drift forward
Do not lean back
Do not drop the weights
mistakes: Turning every set into a full-body swing
Half reps that skip the bottom stretch
Letting the shoulders do the lifting
bicep_curl.tip: Face a wall with your back and elbows lightly touching it — instant strict-curl feedback.

hammer_curl.name: Hammer Curls

video.title: How to Do a Hammer Curl | Arm Workout

hammer_curl.referenceNote: Thickens the arms from the side — hits the brachialis and forearms that regular curls miss.
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
Elbows pinned to your ribs.
Brace your core.
Curl straight up without rotating the wrists.
dos: Keep the neutral grip the whole rep
Keep elbows locked to your sides
Squeeze at the top
Lower under control
donts: Do not rotate into a regular curl mid-rep
Do not swing
Do not let elbows flare out
Do not rush
mistakes: Using momentum to heave the weight
Cutting the top contraction short
Going so heavy the wrists bend
hammer_curl.tip: Try cross-body hammer curls (curl toward the opposite shoulder) for an even stronger brachialis hit.

plank.name: Plank
plank.referenceNote: Not a rest exercise — a full-body tension drill. Squeeze everything.
setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders.
Extend legs back, feet hip-width.
Tuck the pelvis slightly — flat back, no sag.
Look at the floor, neck neutral.
plank.tempo: Hold — breathe steadily behind a braced core.
dos: Squeeze glutes and quads hard
Push the floor away to engage the serratus
Breathe slowly and continuously
Stop the set when form breaks
donts: Do not let hips sag
Do not pike hips to the ceiling
Do not hold your breath
Do not crane your neck up
mistakes: Sagging lower back — the most common plank fail
Shallow breathing or breath-holding
Elbows too far forward, dumping into the shoulders
plank.tip: Cannot hold 45 seconds clean? Do shorter perfect holds — quality seconds beat sloppy minutes.

arnold_press.name: Arnold Press
arnold_press.referenceNote: The rotation hits all three delt heads in one movement — the 3D shoulder builder.
setup: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing you.
Elbows tucked in front, core braced.
Press overhead while rotating palms to face forward.
Reverse the rotation on the way down.
dos: Rotate smoothly through the whole rep
Keep the motion in front of your body
Finish with biceps near ears, palms forward
Control the rotation — no wrist flicking
donts: Do not arch your back
Do not use a weight that kills the rotation
Do not rush the turn
Do not shrug at the top
mistakes: Turning it into a regular press with a token twist
Leaning back to press heavier
Losing core tension and wobbling
arnold_press.tip: Go lighter than your normal press — the rotation is the stimulus, not the load.

close_grip_press.name: Close-Grip DB Press

video.title: How To Do A DUMBBELL CLOSE GRIP FLAT BENCH PRESS (HEX PRESS) | Exercise Demonstration Video

close_grip_press.referenceNote: Dumbbells pressed together — hammers the triceps and inner chest at once.
setup: Lie on the flat bench, dumbbells pressed together over your chest.
Neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Shoulder blades pinched, feet planted.
Lower the pair to your lower chest, elbows tucked.
close_grip_press.tempo: 2-1-2 — keep the inward squeeze the whole time.
dos: Squeeze the dumbbells together the whole set
Tuck elbows close to your ribs
Lower to the lower chest/sternum
Keep constant inward pressure
donts: Do not let the dumbbells separate
Do not flare the elbows
Do not bounce off the chest
Do not lock out aggressively
mistakes: Letting the weights drift apart mid-set
Flaring elbows into a regular press
Rushing and losing the squeeze
close_grip_press.tip: The inward squeeze matters more than the weight — if you cannot keep them touching, go lighter.

front_raise.name: Front Raises

video.channel: Fit Father Project - Fitness For Busy Fathers
video.title: How To Do The Front Raise With Dumbbells OR Kettlebells

front_raise.referenceNote: Direct front-delt work — light weight, strict reps, big payoff.
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Slight bend in the elbows.
Brace your core.
Raise straight in front to shoulder height.
dos: Stop at shoulder height
Keep the torso perfectly still
Slight elbow bend, fixed
Lower slowly
donts: Do not swing the weights up
Do not raise above shoulder height
Do not lean back
Do not shrug
mistakes: Using momentum from the hips
Lifting into the traps' territory above parallel
Going too heavy for an isolation move
front_raise.tip: Alternate arms to keep each rep strict — it halves the cheating opportunities.

prone_y_raise.name: Prone Y-Raises

video.title: How To Perform The Dumbbell Prone Y Raise

prone_y_raise.referenceNote: Lower-trap builder for healthy shoulders and better posture — go embarrassingly light.
setup: Lie chest-down on an incline bench (30-45 degrees).
Arms hang straight down, thumbs pointing up.
Depress shoulder blades — away from ears.
Raise arms into a Y shape until in line with your torso.
dos: Think 'reach long' not 'lift high'
Thumbs to the ceiling
Keep shoulders down away from ears
Pause and squeeze at the top
donts: Do not shrug
Do not arch your lower back to lift higher
Do not use momentum
Do not go heavy — 2 to 5 kg is plenty
mistakes: Shrugging the traps instead of using lower traps
Lifting the chest off the bench
Rushing through with body English
prone_y_raise.tip: Start with no weight at all — if you cannot feel your mid-back working, weight will not help.

russian_twist.name: Russian Twists

video.title: How To Train Your Obliques The Scientific Way

russian_twist.referenceNote: Oblique builder — rotate the torso, not just the arms.
setup: Sit with knees bent, heels lightly on the floor.
Lean back slightly, chest up, back straight.
Hold one dumbbell at your chest.
Rotate your torso to touch the weight down each side.
dos: Rotate from the torso, shoulders turning
Keep the chest up throughout
Move with control, pause each side
Breathe out on each twist
donts: Do not round your lower back
Do not just swing the arms
Do not hold your breath
Do not rush
mistakes: Arms-only movement with a still torso
Rounding the back under fatigue
Going too fast to feel the obliques
russian_twist.tip: Lift your heels an inch off the floor to level up — only once the grounded version is strict.
